name: Bengali
variant: Standard Colloquial Bengali (চলিত ভাষা) as spoken in Bangladesh (Dhaka), in Bengali script; grammar is the shared standard of Bangladesh and West Bengal, and where everyday words differ the Bangladesh word is taught first with the Kolkata word beside it (পানি / জল)
script: Bengali script (বাংলা লিপি), left to right, with vowel signs, conjunct letters, and marks ং ঃ ঁ ৎ; Bengali digits ০–৯
basis: Michigan State University open textbook Basic Bangla (Prasenjit Dey and Rajiv Ranjan), chapter and section order (script; nouns, verbs, pronouns; greetings, introductions, 'be', numerals; possession, needs, likes, verb conjugation; family; daily schedule and future; past, case markers, postpositions; places, adjectives, classifiers; shopping), with classifiers, demonstratives and question words moved early as in the University of Wisconsin elementary Bengali syllabus weeks 1-2
src: Michigan State University open textbook Basic Bangla (Prasenjit Dey and Rajiv Ranjan): full section list of chapters 1-9 from the book's contents navigation (seen on the chapter 5 page), the Open Textbook Library listing of chapter titles, and the chapter 3 learning objectives; read through fetch summaries, section titles only, no lesson text; the book does not say whether it follows Dhaka or Kolkata usage

University of Wisconsin (WISLI) Elementary Bengali syllabus 2022 (PDF), textbook Epar Bangla Opar Bangla: Bangla Across Borders (Salomon, Abedin, Brandl; the textbook itself was not opened): day-by-day plan for weeks 1-2 only (script, ফলা conjuncts, question words, demonstratives, adjectives and numbers, classifiers টা and -জন, আছ-, থাক-, locative and possessive, zero verb); weeks 3-8 were not in the document

Durham University Bengali language courses content summary (PDF): ordered topic and grammar lists for Steps 1 and 2 (including shopping, directions, ordering food, likes, comparing); it says it teaches the 'Dhaka / Calcutta dialect'
note: Variant: none of the sources settles Dhaka against Kolkata (MSU is silent, Durham names both, Wisconsin's textbook is called Bangla Across Borders, which suggests both countries, but it was not opened). Bangladesh was chosen as my own judgment because most Bengali speakers live there and it is the national language there; the grammar taught is the same in both standards, and only greetings, some everyday words (পানি / জল, কয়টা / কটা) and the voice change. The basis textbook is not claimed to follow Dhaka usage. Order: MSU's chapter order is followed for the main line (pronouns and possessives, then greetings, introductions and the zero 'is'; possession with আছে, needs and likes, then verb conjugation; family; future and daily schedule, then telling time; then past, case markers and postpositions; then places and shopping). My changes: demonstratives with -টা, numbers with classifiers and question words come in stage 2, as in Wisconsin weeks 1-2, instead of MSU chapters 8-9, because prices and asking 'where' need them early; MSU's ten conjugation classes (4.4-4.9) are reduced to one present-tense lesson; the present tense, 'where you live' and family come before ordering food and the continuous. Directions, ordering food and comparing are not in MSU's section list; they come from the Durham topic lists, and their place is my own. The present continuous lesson, the separate 'was' lesson and all titles are common course practice and my own judgment. Spelling in titles is my own.
hardest: Spelling against sound: the inherent vowel অ said 'o' or dropped, ই / ঈ and উ / ঊ said the same, শ ষ স all mostly 'sh'
Aspirated against plain (ক / খ, ত / থ) and dental ত দ against retroflex ট ড
Three levels of 'you' (তুই, তুমি, আপনি), each with its own verb ending
Conjunct letters (ক্ষ, স্ত, ন্ত) and classifiers on numbers and nouns (-টা, -জন)

items: bn-vowels
Vowels: অ আ ই ঈ উ ঊ ঋ এ ঐ ও ঔ, and the inherent vowel অ
bn-consonants
Consonants: aspirated খ ঘ ছ ঝ থ ধ ফ ভ against plain; dental ত দ against retroflex ট ড; শ ষ স
bn-vowel-signs
Vowel signs and marks: কা কি কী কু কূ কে কৈ কো কৌ, and ং ঃ ঁ ৎ
bn-conjuncts
Conjuncts and ফলা: ক্ষ, স্ত, ন্ত, and র-ফলা in প্রথম
bn-greetings
Greetings: আসসালামু আলাইকুম, নমস্কার, কেমন আছেন? ভালো আছি; ধন্যবাদ
bn-pronouns
Pronouns and three levels of 'you': আমি, তুই, তুমি, আপনি; সে, তিনি
bn-possessive
Possessive pronouns: আমার, তোমার, আপনার, তার
bn-intro
Introducing yourself with no 'is': আমার নাম …, আমি ছাত্র
bn-questions
Questions and 'not': কী, কে, কার, কোথায়, কেমন; নই, নয়
bn-eta-ota
এটা, ওটা: this and that, and the classifier -টা (বইটা)
bn-numbers
Numbers ১–১০০, classifiers -টা and -জন, and prices: কত টাকা?
bn-ache
আছে and নেই: there is, is at, and having (আমার একটা বই আছে)
bn-need-like
Wants, needs and likes: আমি … চাই, আমার … দরকার, আমার … ভালো লাগে
bn-present
Present simple: আমি করি, তুমি করো, সে করে, আপনি করেন
bn-where
Where you live: the endings -এ / -য় / -তে and থাকা (আমি ঢাকায় থাকি)
bn-family
Family and professions: মা, বাবা, ভাই, বোন; ও, আর, কিন্তু
bn-food
Ordering food: ভাত, মাছ, চা, পানি; … দিন
bn-continuous
Present continuous: করছি, করছ, করছে, করছেন
bn-future
Daily routine and the future: করব, করবে, করবেন
bn-time
Clock time and days: কয়টা বাজে? সাড়ে, সোমবার
bn-past
The simple past: করলাম, করলে, করল, করলেন
bn-chhilo
ছিল: was, were (ছিলাম, ছিলে, ছিল, ছিলেন)
bn-postpositions
Object -কে and postpositions: সাথে, জন্য, কাছে, থেকে
bn-directions
Directions: ডান দিকে, বাঁ দিকে, সোজা; কাছে, দূরে
bn-compare
Describing places and comparing: বড়, ছোট, সুন্দর; এটা ওটার চেয়ে বড়
bn-conjunct-verbs
Noun + করা verbs: কাজ করা, ফোন করা, পছন্দ করা
bn-shopping
Shopping and amounts: এক কেজি, অর্ধেক, দাম কত?
